name: Potato slices / juice
lead: Potato slices or juice is a folk remedy in which thin slices of raw potato, or grated or juiced potato, are placed on the skin under the eyes to lighten dark circles and reduce puffiness. It circulates in home-remedy and beauty communities as a cheap, kitchen-based way to look more rested.

Proponents describe two effects. One is a cooling compress effect, strongest when the slices are chilled, which they say calms morning puffiness. The other is a natural lightening effect on the pigment beneath the eyes, which they attribute to the potato itself.

Dermatology references list the causes of under-eye darkness as thin eyelid skin and underlying anatomy, allergy and rubbing, pigmentation, fatigue, age and sun exposure, and name hydroquinone, caffeine and vitamin C creams, lasers, fillers and fat transfer among treatments; potato is not among the treatments they describe.[1] No clinical study of potato applied to the periorbital area has been published.

chain: Cool, moist slice rests on eyelid
angle.text: People lay chilled potato slices or apply the juice under the eyes hoping for less puffiness and a lighter tone. The cooling effect is the part most often credited for a temporary fresher look; pigment lightening is the claimed longer-term benefit.

infobox: Raw slices, grated pulp or juice
Cold compress; cucumber and tea-bag compresses

paras: The remedy is applied as slices laid over closed eyes for a period of time, or as grated pulp or juice dabbed on the skin. Cold storage before use is common and links it to the cold compress practice.

Under-eye darkness is among the most common appearance complaints, and it has several unrelated causes. Wikipedia lists thin lower-eyelid skin and bone structure, allergy-related rubbing and venous congestion, fatigue, ageing, sun-driven melanin and true periorbital hyperpigmentation.[1] Because people rarely know which cause applies to them, a kitchen remedy that costs almost nothing is attractive as a first thing to try, and potato is one of several household items (alongside cucumber, tea bags and cold spoons) that appear in home-care routines for the area.

The appearance chain proponents describe is short: a cold, moist slice rests on the lids, the area feels cooler and tighter, morning swelling looks reduced, and the eyes read as more awake. The longer-term claim is that regular use fades pigment so that the under-eye area looks lighter.

Practitioners say the slices or juice lighten pigment and reduce swelling. Under-eye puffiness and darkness have many recognised causes, including allergy, fatigue, anatomy and pigmentation, so people report varied results depending on the cause [1].

The cold-compress explanation and the lightening explanation are separate claims. The first rests on temperature and moisture and could apply to any chilled slice; the second attributes an effect to compounds in the potato itself.

Cold compresses are used generally to reduce swelling after soft-tissue injury and surgery; Wikipedia describes them as combining cold with pressure to limit fluid leaking into tissue.[4] The same article notes that the evidence for some cold-therapy uses is debated and that ice applied directly to skin can cause a cold burn, which is why ice wraps usually include a protective layer.[4] Potato slices used for under-eye puffiness are usually chilled rather than frozen, and the cooling is the part that practitioners most often credit for a short-lived fresher look.

Raw potatoes contain glycoalkaloids, chiefly solanine and chaconine. Levels are highest in the skin, rise when tubers are exposed to light and turn green, and are higher in damaged or aged tubers; properly grown and stored tubers contain only small amounts [2].

A 2023 review of home remedies in dermatology describes them as widely available and inexpensive and reports that authors found promising results with limited evidence, calling for well-controlled studies with larger samples.[5] The review does not discuss potato, and it lists irritation among documented risks of other raw household items such as onion juice and vinegar, which illustrates why dermatologists treat contact reactions to raw plant material as a general consideration.[5] Hydroquinone, once used in lightening products, lost its over-the-counter approval from the US FDA in 2006, and Wikipedia lists caffeine and vitamin C creams, lasers, intense pulsed light, fillers and fat transfer as treatments researched for the periorbital area.[1]

No study has examined how potato affects eyelid skin. Because it is a raw plant material applied near the eyes, people with sensitive skin or allergy tendencies may react, and glycoalkaloid content is greater in green or sprouting potatoes [2].

Wikipedia's solanine article describes the compound as a toxic glycoalkaloid found in nightshades, concentrated in or near potato skin and raised by light exposure, damage, sprouting and poor storage.[3] Its poisoning cases concern eating green or damaged potatoes, and the article does not describe topical exposure.[3] Raw potato intended for under-eye use is typically a fresh, peeled slice, and whether skin contact near the eyes matters has not been studied.

lore.intro: Potato slices are mentioned in home-remedy and beauty circles as one of several kitchen options for tired eyes, with proponents describing cooling and lightening.

claims.believers: Proponents say compounds in raw potato lighten pigment under the eyes with regular use.
claims.experts: Dermatology references list hydroquinone, caffeine, vitamin C, lasers, fillers and fat transfer for dark circles and do not list potato; no trial of potato on periorbital skin has been published.[1]

claims.claim: Chilled potato slices reduce under-eye puffiness
claims.believers: Users describe a cooling, tightening effect on the lids that makes the eyes look less swollen.
claims.experts: Cold compression is used for swelling after injury and surgery, though evidence for some uses is debated; no study has tested potato slices for eyelid puffiness.[4]

claims.claim: Raw potato on the skin is harmless because it is a food
claims.believers: Proponents point to potato's ordinary place in the diet.
claims.experts: Raw potato contains glycoalkaloids that rise in green, sprouting or damaged tubers, and safety on skin near the eyes has not been studied.[2][3]

card.summary: Raw potato slices or juice applied under the eyes as a folk lightener; no studies of it for dark circles were found.
card.note: Raw potato contains glycoalkaloids; no human trials for this use.

quick.overview:
Raw potato slices or grated-potato juice are a folk remedy for dark circles and puffiness. Proponents describe them as a natural lightener and cooling compress.

No published study was found testing potato for this purpose.
quick.mechanism: Believers say compounds in raw potato lighten pigment, and slices applied cold may soothe the area. These mechanisms have not been tested on under-eye skin.
quick.risks: No safety data were found for this use. Raw potatoes contain glycoalkaloids such as solanine and chaconine, which rise in green or damaged tubers; whether skin application matters has not been studied. Contact irritation is possible with any raw plant material.
